title: KeyInclusion - a key laid on top of the previous one (KS-1)
description: An agent key is never replaced; a new key is laid on top of the previous one, and every key in the set stays valid. The linkage is a chain, joined by the predecessor hash and walked one link at a time; the result is a set of simultaneously valid keys. The words succession, inheritance, rotation and replacement are wrong here: an act signed by the first key stays valid when the set already holds many more. Introduced in core version 2.

predecessor.description: The hash of the previous link: the AgentBinding for the first inclusion, the previous KeyInclusion after that. A hash rather than a kid, because the hash pins the whole previous link - its key, its offset and its signatures - while a reference by name would leave the rest of the link substitutable without breaking the chain.

offset_ms.description: Milliseconds since the container's genesis. Not a timestamp and MUST NOT be displayed as a date: without anchors it does not convert to absolute time at all. Its force comes from being bracketed between two anchors.

signatures.description: Signed by the key of the PREVIOUS link, not by the key being added: a signature by the key being added would prove nothing, since whoever generated it a second ago holds it.
